[bug] Fix subcategory visualization in report graphs
## Observed Behavior (OB)
In reports, the category selector lets you check or uncheck individual subcategories, but doing so doesn't change the graphs or tables. Reports always roll subcategories up into their parent category's row, so you only ever see the parent's total. Toggling a subcategory either does nothing or only changes the parent's total. You can't see a subcategory as its own bar, slice or line.

## Expected Behavior (EB)
You should be able to check and uncheck subcategories in a report to change what the user graph shows, so you can see how much each subcategory contributes instead of only seeing the parent category total.

## Steps to Reproduce (S2R)
1. On the budget page, add a subcategory to a category
2. On the accounts page, make a payment that goes towards said subcategory
3. On the reports page, make a new custom report
4. Within the custom report, select only the parent category and the subcategory
5. The subcategory isn't shown whether subcategory is selected or not.

## Additional Information

<img width="1728" height="995" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7501081f-8760-4c7e-b262-32eae19bfd26" />
<img width="1728" height="995" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a2e82c67-43e5-4ae2-8c59-94168b87b5a4" />


## Acceptance Criteria
**Subcategory selection in reports**
1. Unchecking a subcategory removes its amount from the report, both from the parent's rolled-up total and from any row of its own.
2. A checked subcategory can be shown as its own item (bar, donut slice, line or table row) when the report is grouped by category, instead of always being merged into the parent.
3. When subcategories are shown on their own, the parent's row is not double counted. The parent shows only its own transactions, or the subcategories are clearly nested under it.
4. Report totals stay correct in every combination of parent and subcategory checked or unchecked.
5. Behavior is consistent across the custom report graph types (Bar, Stacked Bar, Line, Donut, Table) and the dashboard widgets that use them.
6. (Optional) Add a toggle such as "Show subcategories" so users can pick between the rolled-up parent view (today's behavior) and the expanded subcategory view.

## Out of Scope
- Changes to how subcategories are created or nested on the budget page.
- Reports that don't group by category (for example Net Worth or Cash Flow).

## Open Questions
- Should the expanded subcategory view be the default, or should the current rolled-up view stay the default behind a toggle?
- If the parent is unchecked but some of its subcategories are checked, should those subcategories still show up as their own rows?

## Rough Scope
Medium: The roll-up logic lives in `packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/subcategories.ts` (`getRolledUpCategoryIds`, `getNestedSubcategoryIds`) and is used by the report spreadsheets (`custom-spreadsheet.ts`, `grouped-spreadsheet.ts`). The selector UI is in `CategorySelector.tsx`. The main work is making the spreadsheets respect which subcategories are selected and emit separate rows for them without double counting. `subcategories.test.ts` should be extended to cover the new cases.

## Source
Found while testing reports with nested subcategories. Follows up on the subcategory roll-up behavior added to reports.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-27 23:26:13Z)**_

Yes. The cause is `expandSubcategoryConditions` in [subcategories.ts:93-125](packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/subcategories.ts#L93-L125). It's working as designed, but that design conflicts with the category selector, and `getRolledUpCategoryIds` then adds the extra amounts into the parent's total.

**What happens when you uncheck a subcategory**

1. The selector turns your checked boxes into a single filter. `setSelectedCategories` in [CustomReport.tsx:219-264](packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/reports/CustomReport.tsx#L219-L264) writes `{ field: 'category', op: 'oneOf', value: [checked ids] }`. With the parent checked and the subcategory unchecked, that's `oneOf [parent]`.
2. Before querying, [custom-spreadsheet.ts:134](packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/custom-spreadsheet.ts#L134) passes that filter through `expandSubcategoryConditions`. Any parent id gets all its subcategories added (`withSubcategories`, lines 101-105), so `oneOf [parent]` becomes `oneOf [parent, sub]`. The subcategory you unchecked is back in the query.
3. The subcategory never gets a row of its own, because `getNestedSubcategoryIds` removes it ([custom-spreadsheet.ts:108-111](packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/custom-spreadsheet.ts#L108-L111)). The parent's row matches on `getRolledUpCategoryIds(parent)`, which is `[parent, sub]` ([custom-spreadsheet.ts:201-208](packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/custom-spreadsheet.ts#L201-L208) and line 308). So the unchecked subcategory's spending lands in the parent's total.

The filter can't tell "the user picked this parent in a rule filter" apart from "the user checked this parent's box and deliberately unchecked its children". It treats both as the whole family.

**Related cases from the same cause**

- **Subcategory checked, parent unchecked:** with `oneOf [sub]` nothing is expanded, so the subcategory's transactions are fetched. But it still has no row of its own, and the matching in step 3 has no check on whether the parent was selected. Its amount can still turn up under the parent, and it is never shown separately.
- **A `notOneOf [parent]` filter** (the selector keeps using `notOneOf` when that filter already exists, lines 245-250): this expands to exclude every subcategory too, even ones that are still checked.

**Where to fix it.** For acceptance criteria 1 and 4, the selector's filter should leave out exactly the ids that are checked. One option is to skip `expandSubcategoryConditions` for the condition that `setSelectedCategories` owns. Another is to make that condition list the subcategories explicitly, since the selector already knows the full checked set. Either way, the parent's roll-up in `getRolledUpCategoryIds` should only include subcategories that are selected. Criterion 2 (subcategories as their own rows) means changing `getNestedSubcategoryIds` so it doesn't remove selected subcategories when an expanded view is on, and the parent row then has to match only its own id so nothing is counted twice. [grouped-spreadsheet.ts:61](packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/grouped-spreadsheet.ts#L61) and `:149` use the same pattern and would need the same change.

I worked this out by reading the code; I haven't reproduced it in the app or written a failing test. I can add a case to `subcategories.test.ts` that shows it if you'd like.

import type {
  balanceTypeOpType,
  CategoryEntity,
  CategoryGroupEntity,
  RuleConditionEntity,
} from '@actual-app/core/types/models';
import type { SyncedPrefs } from '@actual-app/core/types/prefs';

import type { QueryDataEntity } from '#components/reports/ReportOptions';
import { aqlQuery } from '#queries/aqlQuery';

import { fetchBudgetData } from './budgetDataQuery';
import { makeQuery } from './makeQuery';
import { hideSubcategoriesOfHiddenParents } from './subcategories';

type FetchSpreadsheetQueryDataProps = {
  balanceTypeOp: balanceTypeOpType | undefined;
  startDate: string;
  endDate: string;
  interval: string;
  categories: CategoryEntity[];
  categoryGroups: CategoryGroupEntity[];
  conditions: RuleConditionEntity[];
  conditionsOp: string;
  conditionsOpKey: string;
  filters: unknown[];
  budgetType?: SyncedPrefs['budgetType'];
};

type QueryData = { assets: QueryDataEntity[]; debts: QueryDataEntity[] };

export async function fetchSpreadsheetQueryData(
  props: FetchSpreadsheetQueryDataProps,
): Promise<QueryData> {
  const { assets, debts } = await fetchRows(props);

  return {
    assets: hideSubcategoriesOfHiddenParents(assets, props.categoryGroups),
    debts: hideSubcategoriesOfHiddenParents(debts, props.categoryGroups),
  };
}

async function fetchRows({
  balanceTypeOp,
  startDate,
  endDate,
  interval,
  categories,
  categoryGroups,
  conditions,
  conditionsOp,
  conditionsOpKey,
  filters,
  budgetType,
}: FetchSpreadsheetQueryDataProps): Promise<QueryData> {
  if (balanceTypeOp === 'totalBudgeted') {
    return fetchBudgetData({
      startDate,
      endDate,
      interval,
      categories,
      categoryGroups,
      conditions,
      conditionsOp: conditionsOp === 'or' ? 'or' : 'and',
      budgetType,
    });
  }

  const [assets, debts] = await Promise.all([
    aqlQuery(
      makeQuery(
        'assets',
        startDate,
        endDate,
        interval,
        conditionsOpKey,
        filters,
      ),
    ).then(({ data }) => data),
    aqlQuery(
      makeQuery(
        'debts',
        startDate,
        endDate,
        interval,
        conditionsOpKey,
        filters,
      ),
    ).then(({ data }) => data),
  ]);

  return { assets, debts };
}

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-27 23:27:49Z)**_

There's one other cause, and it's a separate mechanism from the filter. It's what makes the subcategory never appear in the report (step 5 of the issue). The filter expansion is still the only reason an unchecked subcategory's money gets fetched.

**1. Parent rows always include every subcategory, whatever is checked**

Each place that builds a parent's row adds in the full list of subcategories without checking the selection:
- [custom-spreadsheet.ts:201](packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/custom-spreadsheet.ts#L201) and [:308](packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/custom-spreadsheet.ts#L308), through `getRolledUpCategoryIds`.
- [grouped-spreadsheet.ts:173](packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/grouped-spreadsheet.ts#L173), which does `calculateCategory(item, [item.id, ...subcategoryIds])`.

On its own, this wouldn't pull in an unchecked subcategory, because its transactions wouldn't be fetched without the filter expansion. But it does cause a different wrong result. If you uncheck the parent and check only the subcategory, the subcategory's spending still appears, labelled with the parent's name. Every category gets a row, empty ones are dropped later, and the parent's row picks up the subcategory's amounts.

**2. Subcategories never get a row of their own**

`getNestedSubcategoryIds` drops every subcategory from the rows ([custom-spreadsheet.ts:108-111](packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/custom-spreadsheet.ts#L108-L111), [grouped-spreadsheet.ts:149](packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/grouped-spreadsheet.ts#L149)), so the subcategory can't show up as its own bar, slice or line. This is deliberate, to avoid counting amounts twice. Combined with #1, the only visible effect of checking or unchecking a subcategory is a change in the parent's total, which is what the issue describes.

**3. Clicking through to transactions has the same problem**

When you click a parent's bar or slice, `showActivity` adds all its subcategories to the transaction filter (`includeSubcategories` defaults to `true`, [showActivity.ts:63-70](packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/graphs/showActivity.ts#L63-L70)). It also runs the report's filters through `expandSubcategoryConditions` again (line 104). So even after the spreadsheets are fixed, the transaction list would still include unchecked subcategories unless this is changed too.

**Ruled out:**
- **The selector** ([CategorySelector.tsx:256-267](packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/CategorySelector.tsx#L256-L267)): unchecking a subcategory removes only that one id. One quirk: re-checking a parent re-checks all its subcategories, including any you unchecked on purpose.
- **Budgeted reports and dashboard widgets:** budgeted reports get the already-expanded filter ([fetchSpreadsheetQueryData.ts:56-66](packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/fetchSpreadsheetQueryData.ts#L56-L66)), and dashboard widgets use the same spreadsheet code. Neither adds a separate cause; they're fixed by the same changes.

So a full fix for #100 touches four places:
- the filter expansion;
- the parent roll-ups, which should include only checked subcategories;
- removing subcategory rows, so checked subcategories can show on their own;
- the transaction click-through.

As before, this comes from reading the code; I haven't reproduced it in the app.

**How should users switch between seeing parent totals and seeing each subcategory on its own (acceptance criteria 2 and 6)?**

Options:
- **Saved toggle, off (Recommended)** - Add a 'Show subcategories' option that is saved with each custom report. It starts off, so existing reports and dashboard widgets look the same as today. Needs a database migration and new report fields.
- **Saved toggle, on** - Same saved option, but new reports start with subcategories shown on their own. Existing saved reports stay rolled up.
- **Always separate** - No toggle. Whenever the report is grouped by category, subcategories always get their own rows and the parent shows only its own transactions. Simplest, but changes how every existing report looks.
- **Unsaved toggle** - A toggle that lasts only for the current session and isn't saved with the report. No migration, but dashboard widgets can't use it.

**If the parent is unchecked but some of its subcategories are checked, what should the report show (an open question in the issue)?**

Options:
- **Subcategory gets own row (Recommended)** - Each checked subcategory appears as its own row, even in the rolled-up view, so its amount is never shown under the name of a parent you unchecked.
- **Roll into parent row** - Keep showing the subcategory's amount under the parent's name, even though the parent is unchecked (today's behavior).
- **Hide it** - Leave the subcategory out of the report entirely while its parent is unchecked.

**Custom reports turn the category checkboxes into a single 'category is one of' filter, which looks the same as one typed into the filter bar. To fix the bug, custom reports would apply that filter exactly as written. Is that OK?**

Options:
- **Apply as written (Recommended)** - In custom reports, the single category filter covers exactly the categories listed, which is also what the checkboxes show. Choosing a parent in the checkboxes still ticks its subcategories, so nothing changes for normal use. Other reports (Spending, Cash Flow, etc.) keep including subcategories.
- **Mark checkbox filters** - Tag filters created by the checkboxes and apply only those exactly as written. A filter typed into the filter bar would still include the parent's subcategories. More code, and older saved reports would need special handling.


**Answer:** Saved toggle, off (Recommended), Subcategory gets own row (Recommended), Apply as written (Recommended)

Design a detailed implementation plan (read-only; do not edit files) for a bug fix in the Actual Budget monorepo at /Users/james/ActualBudget/actual-budget (read AGENTS.md for conventions). Return concrete per-file changes with function names and approximate line numbers, plus a test list.

## The bug (issue #100)
In custom reports (Reports → new custom report, grouped by Category), the category selector lets you check/uncheck subcategories (categories with `parent_id`), but:
- Unchecking a subcategory doesn't remove its amount: it's still added to the parent's total.
- A subcategory is never shown as its own bar/slice/line/row.

## Root causes already confirmed
1. `packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/reports/CustomReport.tsx` `setSelectedCategories` (~L219-264) turns the checked boxes into a single `{field:'category', op:'oneOf', value:[checked ids]}` condition (or updates an existing `notOneOf`). `useSelectedCategories` (~L73) reads it back. `isComplexCategoryCondition` (~L204-217) disables the selector when there are 2+ category conditions, category_group conditions, or contains/matches/etc.
2. `packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/subcategories.ts` `expandSubcategoryConditions` expands any parent id in category is/oneOf/isNot/notOneOf conditions to the whole family. `custom-spreadsheet.ts` (~L134) and `grouped-spreadsheet.ts` (~L61) call it on all conditions, so `oneOf [parent]` becomes `oneOf [parent, sub]` and the unchecked sub is fetched again. Budgeted mode (`fetchSpreadsheetQueryData` → `fetchBudgetData`/`filterCategoriesByConditions` in budgetDataQuery.ts) receives the same expanded conditions.
3. Rows: `custom-spreadsheet.ts` drops every subcategory from `rowItems` via `getNestedSubcategoryIds` (~L104-111), and parent rows match `getRolledUpCategoryIds(parent)` = [parent, ...all subs] (~L201, ~L308, through `recalculate.ts` `categoryIds`). `grouped-spreadsheet.ts` (~L142-190) builds top-level `categories` with parents rolled up, plus a nested `subcategories` list (each sub, plus an 'unallocated'/'Not in a subcategory' row for the parent's own transactions) that nothing adds up.
4. Clicking through: `packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/graphs/showActivity.ts` has `includeSubcategories = true` by default, which adds all subcategory ids to the clicked parent (~L63-70), and it also runs `expandSubcategoryConditions(filters, ...)` again (~L104). Callers are in DonutGraph.tsx, tableGraph/ReportTableRow.tsx, and probably BarGraph/StackedBarGraph/LineGraph/AreaGraph. Check how they pass `filters` and `includeSubcategories`.
5. `CategorySelector.tsx` is fine: ticking a parent ticks its family, and unticking a sub removes only that sub.

## Decisions the user made
A. Add a **saved** custom-report option, "Show subcategories" (default **off**, so existing reports look unchanged). It needs to go through the same path as `showUncategorized`: `packages/loot-core/src/types/models/reports.ts` (CustomReportEntity ~L19 and the DB row type ~L163), `packages/loot-core/src/server/db/types/index.ts` ~L267, `packages/loot-core/src/server/reports/app.ts` (~L47, ~L74 mapping), `packages/loot-core/src/server/aql/schema/index.ts` ~L174, plus a new migration in `packages/loot-core/migrations/` (check the latest file names for timestamp format; SQL `ALTER TABLE custom_reports ADD COLUMN ...`). Find and include the desktop-client side: `defaultReport` in ReportOptions.ts, CustomReport.tsx state/session/save/`onReportChange`/dirty detection, the ReportSidebar.tsx UI (look at how the show-empty/off-budget/uncategorized/hidden toggles are rendered; only show the new one when groupBy is Category, or Category+Group if that makes sense), GetCardData.tsx (dashboard widgets), and any other place that lists every report field (search for `showUncategorized` and `show_uncategorized` across packages, including tests, the api package and any sync/import code).
B. When the parent is unchecked but some subs are checked, each checked sub gets its **own row even in the rolled-up view**. A parent row then rolls up only its checked subs.
C. In custom reports, the single selector-owned category condition (the one `useSelectedCategories` reflects, i.e. when not `isComplexCategoryCondition`) is applied **exactly as written**, with no family expansion. Other conditions (complex case) still go through `expandSubcategoryConditions`. Other reports (spending, cash-flow, etc.) are unchanged.

## Required behavior (acceptance criteria)
1. Unchecking a sub removes its amount everywhere (the parent's roll-up and any row of its own).
2. With the toggle on and grouped by category, every checked sub is its own item, and the parent row shows only its own transactions. In the grouped/table view, prefer keeping the existing nesting in `subcategories` if the table already renders it; work out how it renders today.
3. No double counting: totals (`totalAssets`, `totalDebts`, `totalTotals`, `totalSpent`, `intervalData` sums, legend) stay correct for every combination of parent/sub checked and toggle on/off.
4. Consistent across Bar, Stacked Bar, Line, Area, Donut, Table and dashboard widgets (GetCardData).
5. Clicking through to transactions matches what the row adds up.

# AGENTS.md - Guide for AI Agents Working with Actual Budget

This guide provides comprehensive information for AI agents (like Cursor) working with the Actual Budget codebase.

## Project Overview

**Actual Budget** is a local-first personal finance tool written in TypeScript/JavaScript. It's 100% free and open-source with synchronization capabilities across devices.

- **Repository**: https://github.com/actualbudget/actual
- **Community Docs**: Documentation is part of the monorepo at `packages/docs/`. Published at https://actualbudget.org/docs
- **License**: MIT
- **Primary Language**: TypeScript (with React)
- **Build System**: Yarn 4 workspaces (monorepo)

## Quick Start Commands

### Essential Commands (Run from Root)

```bash
# Type checking (ALWAYS run before committing)
yarn typecheck

# Linting and formatting (with auto-fix)
yarn lint:fix

# Run all tests
yarn test

# Start development server (browser)
yarn start

# Start with sync server
yarn start:server-dev

# Start desktop app development
yarn start:desktop
```

### Important Rules

- **ALWAYS run yarn commands from the root directory** - never run them in child workspaces
- Use `yarn workspace <workspace-name> run <command>` for workspace-specific tasks
- Tests run once and exit by default (using `vitest --run`)

### ⚠️ PR titles must start with `[AI]`

Every pull request title must be prefixed with `[AI]` — you have to apply it
yourself. See [PR and Commit Rules](.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md).

### Task Orchestration with Lage

The project uses **[lage](https://microsoft.github.io/lage/)** (a task runner for JavaScript monorepos) to efficiently run tests and other tasks across multiple workspaces:

- **Parallel execution**: Runs tests in parallel across workspaces for faster feedback
- **Smart caching**: Caches test results to skip unchanged packages (cached in `.lage/` directory)
- **Dependency awareness**: Understands workspace dependencies and execution order
- **Continues on error**: Uses `--continue` flag to run all packages even if one fails

**Lage Commands:**

```bash
# Run all tests across all packages
yarn test                    # Equivalent to: lage test --continue

# Run tests without cache (for debugging/CI)
yarn test:debug              # Equivalent to: lage test --no-cache --continue
```

Configuration is in `lage.config.js` at the project root.

## Architecture & Package Structure

### Core Packages

#### 1. **loot-core** (`packages/loot-core/`)

The core application logic that runs on any platform.

- Business logic, database operations, and calculations
- Platform-agnostic code
- Exports for both browser and node environments
- Test commands:

  ```bash
  # Run all loot-core tests
  yarn workspace @actual-app/core run test

  # Or run tests across all packages using lage
  yarn test
  ```

#### 2. **desktop-client** (`packages/desktop-client/` - aliased as `@actual-app/web`)

The React-based UI for web and desktop.

- React components using functional programming patterns
- E2E tests using Playwright
- Vite for bundling
- Commands:

  ```bash
  # Development
  yarn workspace @actual-app/web start:browser

  # Build
  yarn workspace @actual-app/web build

  # E2E tests
  yarn workspace @actual-app/web e2e

  # Visual regression tests
  yarn workspace @actual-app/web vrt
  ```

#### 3. **desktop-electron** (`packages/desktop-electron/`)

Electron wrapper for the desktop application.

- Window management and native OS integration
- E2E tests for Electron-specific features

#### 4. **api** (`packages/api/` - aliased as `@actual-app/api`)

Public API for programmatic access to Actual.

- Node.js API
- Designed for integrations and automation
- Commands:

  ```bash
  # Build
  yarn workspace @actual-app/api build

  # Run tests
  yarn workspace @actual-app/api test

  # Or use lage to run all tests
  yarn test
  ```

#### 5. **sync-server** (`packages/sync-server/` - aliased as `@actual-app/sync-server`)

Synchronization server for multi-device support.

- Express-based server
- Currently transitioning to TypeScript (mostly JavaScript)
- Commands:
  ```bash
  yarn workspace @actual-app/sync-server start
  ```

```text
import { send } from '@actual-app/core/platform/client/connection';
import { nestCategories } from '@actual-app/core/shared/categories';
import type {
  CategoryGroupEntity,
  RuleConditionEntity,
} from '@actual-app/core/types/models';

import type { QueryDataEntity } from '#components/reports/ReportOptions';

// Maps each parent category to its subcategories' ids, nested the same way
// the budget page nests them: a subcategory whose parent is missing or in
// another group is reported as a top-level category instead.
export function getSubcategoryIdsByParent(
  categoryGroups: Pick<CategoryGroupEntity, 'categories'>[],
): Map<string, string[]> {
  const subcategoryIds = new Map<string, string[]>();
  for (const group of categoryGroups) {
    for (const parent of nestCategories(group.categories ?? [])) {
      if (parent.subcategories.length > 0) {
        subcategoryIds.set(
          parent.id,
          parent.subcategories.map(sub => sub.id),
        );
      }
    }
  }
  return subcategoryIds;
}

// The categories a report row adds up. A parent's row includes everything
// its subcategories hold, so it covers its own id and theirs. Other rows
// get undefined and match on their own id as usual.
export function getRolledUpCategoryIds(
  id: string | undefined,
  subcategoryIdsByParent: Map<string, string[]>,
): string[] | undefined {
  const subcategoryIds = id ? subcategoryIdsByParent.get(id) : undefined;
  return subcategoryIds && id ? [id, ...subcategoryIds] : undefined;
}

// Categories that are reported inside their parent's row rather than as a
// row of their own. Totals add up top-level rows only, so leaving these
// out is what keeps a subcategory from being counted twice.
export function getNestedSubcategoryIds(
  subcategoryIdsByParent: Map<string, string[]>,
): Set<string> {
  return new Set([...subcategoryIdsByParent.values()].flat());
}

// Subcategories of hidden parents, which the budget page hides along with
// their parent.
export function getSubcategoryIdsOfHiddenParents(
  categoryGroups: Pick<CategoryGroupEntity, 'categories'>[],
): Set<string> {
  const hiddenParentIds = new Set(
    categoryGroups
      .flatMap(group => group.categories ?? [])
      .filter(cat => cat.hidden)
      .map(cat => cat.id),
  );
  const ids = new Set<string>();
  for (const [parentId, subcategoryIds] of getSubcategoryIdsByParent(
    categoryGroups,
  )) {
    if (hiddenParentIds.has(parentId)) {
      subcategoryIds.forEach(id => ids.add(id));
    }
  }
  return ids;
}

// Marks rows of a hidden parent's subcategories as hidden, so they're left
// out of reports the same way the parent is.
export function hideSubcategoriesOfHiddenParents(
  rows: QueryDataEntity[],
  categoryGroups: Pick<CategoryGroupEntity, 'categories'>[],
): QueryDataEntity[] {
  const hiddenIds = getSubcategoryIdsOfHiddenParents(categoryGroups);
  if (hiddenIds.size === 0) {
    return rows;
  }
  return rows.map(row =>
    row.category && hiddenIds.has(row.category)
      ? { ...row, categoryHidden: true }
      : row,
  );
}

// A report filter on a parent category covers its subcategories too, the
// same way the parent's report row includes them: "is" and "one of" match
// the whole family, "is not" and "not one of" leave the whole family out.
// Filters on the category's name are left as they are.
export function expandSubcategoryConditions(
  conditions: RuleConditionEntity[],
  categoryGroups: Pick<CategoryGroupEntity, 'categories'>[],
): RuleConditionEntity[] {
  const subcategoryIdsByParent = getSubcategoryIdsByParent(categoryGroups);
  if (subcategoryIdsByParent.size === 0) {
    return conditions;
  }
  const withSubcategories = (ids: string[]) => [
    ...new Set(
      ids.flatMap(id => [id, ...(subcategoryIdsByParent.get(id) ?? [])]),
    ),
  ];

  return conditions.map(cond => {
    if (
      cond.field !== 'category' ||
      !['is', 'isNot', 'oneOf', 'notOneOf'].includes(cond.op)
    ) {
      return cond;
    }
    const ids = Array.isArray(cond.value) ? cond.value : [cond.value];
    if (!ids.some(id => subcategoryIdsByParent.has(id))) {
      return cond;
    }
    const excludes = cond.op === 'isNot' || cond.op === 'notOneOf';
    return {
      ...cond,
      op: excludes ? 'notOneOf' : 'oneOf',
      value: withSubcategories(ids),
    };
  });
}

// expandSubcategoryConditions for reports that don't already have the
// categories loaded; only fetches them when there's a category filter.
export async function includeSubcategoriesInConditions(
  conditions: RuleConditionEntity[],
): Promise<RuleConditionEntity[]> {
  if (!conditions.some(cond => cond.field === 'category')) {
    return conditions;
  }
  const { grouped } = await send('get-categories');
  return expandSubcategoryConditions(conditions, grouped);
}

   152	      categoryGroups: categories.grouped,

    23	  startDate: string;
    24	  endDate: string;
    25	  // When set, the row adds up these categories instead of matching on
    26	  // `item.id`; a parent category passes its own id and its subcategories'.
    27	  categoryIds?: string[];
    28	};
    29	
    30	export function recalculate({
    31	  item,
    32	  intervals,
    33	  assets,
    34	  debts,
    35	  groupByLabel,
    36	  showOffBudget,
    37	  showHiddenCategories,
    38	  showUncategorized,
    39	  startDate,
    40	  endDate,
    41	  categoryIds,
    42	}: recalculateProps): GroupedEntity {
    43	  let totalAssets = 0;
    44	  let totalDebts = 0;
    45	  let totalSpent = 0;
    46	  // Budget rows also carry what each category spent.
    47	  const hasSpent = [...assets, ...debts].some(row => row.spent !== undefined);
    48	  const sumSpent = (rows: QueryDataEntity[]) =>
    49	    rows.reduce((a, v) => a + (v.spent ?? 0), 0);
    50	  const groupsByCategory =
    51	    groupByLabel === 'category' || groupByLabel === 'categoryGroup';
    52	  const matchesItem = (row: QueryDataEntity) =>
    53	    categoryIds
    54	      ? categoryIds.includes(row.category)
    55	      : row[groupByLabel] === (item.id ?? null) ||
    56	        (item.uncategorized_id && groupsByCategory);
    57	
    58	  const intervalData = intervals.reduce(
    59	    (arr: IntervalEntity[], intervalItem, index) => {
    60	      const last = arr.length === 0 ? null : arr[arr.length - 1];
    61	
    62	      const assetRows = filterHiddenItems(
    63	        item,
    64	        assets,
    65	        showOffBudget,
    66	        showHiddenCategories,
    67	        showUncategorized,
    68	        groupsByCategory,
    69	      ).filter(asset => asset.date === intervalItem && matchesItem(asset));
    70	      const intervalAssets = assetRows.reduce((a, v) => a + v.amount, 0);
    71	      totalAssets += intervalAssets;
    72	
    73	      const debtRows = filterHiddenItems(
    74	        item,
    75	        debts,
    76	        showOffBudget,
    77	        showHiddenCategories,
    78	        showUncategorized,
    79	        groupsByCategory,
    80	      ).filter(debt => debt.date === intervalItem && matchesItem(debt));
    81	      const intervalDebts = debtRows.reduce((a, v) => a + v.amount, 0);
    82	      totalDebts += intervalDebts;
    83	
    84	      // Each budget row is in exactly one of the two lists, so this
    85	      // counts every row's spending once.
    86	      const intervalSpent = sumSpent(assetRows) + sumSpent(debtRows);
    87	      totalSpent += intervalSpent;
    88	
    89	      const intervalTotals = intervalAssets + intervalDebts;
    90	
    91	      const change = last ? intervalTotals - last.totalTotals : 0;
    92	
    93	      arr.push({
    94	        date: intervalItem,
    95	        totalAssets: intervalAssets,
    96	        totalDebts: intervalDebts,
    97	        netAssets: intervalTotals > 0 ? intervalTotals : 0,
    98	        netDebts: intervalTotals < 0 ? intervalTotals : 0,
    99	        totalTotals: intervalTotals,
   100	        totalBudgeted: intervalTotals,
   101	        ...(hasSpent && { totalSpent: intervalSpent }),
   102	        change,
   103	        intervalStartDate: index === 0 ? startDate : intervalItem,
   104	        intervalEndDate:
   105	          index + 1 === intervals.length
   106	            ? endDate
   107	            : monthUtils.subDays(intervals[index + 1], 1),
   108	      });
   109	
   110	      return arr;
   111	    },
   112	    [],
   113	  );
   114	
   115	  const totalTotals = totalAssets + totalDebts;
   116	
   117	  return {
   118	    id: item.id || '',
   119	    name: item.name,
   120	    uncategorizedId: item.uncategorized_id,
   121	    totalAssets,
   122	    totalDebts,
   123	    netAssets: totalTotals > 0 ? totalTotals : 0,
   124	    netDebts: totalTotals < 0 ? totalTotals : 0,
   125	    totalTotals,
   126	    totalBudgeted: totalTotals,
   127	    ...(hasSpent && { totalSpent }),
   128	    intervalData,
   129	  };
   130	}

      sortByOp: report.sortBy,
      dateFormat,

    endDate,

    budgetType,

```text
import React, { useRef } from 'react';
import type { CSSProperties, UIEvent } from 'react';

import { styles } from '@actual-app/components/styles';
import type {
  DataEntity,
  RuleConditionEntity,
} from '@actual-app/core/types/models';

import { AreaGraph } from './graphs/AreaGraph';
import { BarGraph } from './graphs/BarGraph';
import { BarLineGraph } from './graphs/BarLineGraph';
import { DonutGraph } from './graphs/DonutGraph';
import { LineGraph } from './graphs/LineGraph';
import { StackedBarGraph } from './graphs/StackedBarGraph';
import { ReportTable } from './graphs/tableGraph/ReportTable';
import { ReportOptions } from './ReportOptions';

type ChooseGraphProps = {
  data: DataEntity;
  filters?: RuleConditionEntity[];
  mode: string;
  graphType: string;
  balanceType: string;
  groupBy: string;
  interval: string;
  setScrollWidth?: (value: number) => void;
  viewLabels?: boolean;
  compact: boolean;
  style?: CSSProperties;
  showHiddenCategories?: boolean;
  showOffBudget?: boolean;
  showTrendLines?: boolean;
  showTooltip?: boolean;
  intervalsCount: number;
};

export function ChooseGraph({
  data,
  filters = [],
  mode,
  graphType,
  balanceType,
  groupBy,
  interval,
  setScrollWidth,
  viewLabels = false,
  compact,
  style,
  showHiddenCategories = false,
  showOffBudget = false,
  showTrendLines = false,
  showTooltip = true,
  intervalsCount,
}: ChooseGraphProps) {
  const graphStyle = compact
    ? { ...style }
    : { flexGrow: 1, overflow: 'hidden' };
  const balanceTypeOp =
    ReportOptions.balanceTypeMap.get(balanceType) || 'totalDebts';

  const saveScrollWidth = (value: number) => {
    setScrollWidth?.(value || 0);
  };

  const rowStyle: CSSProperties = compact
    ? { flex: '0 0 20px', height: 20 }
    : {};
  const compactStyle: CSSProperties = compact ? { ...styles.tinyText } : {};

  const headerScrollRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const listScrollRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const totalScrollRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);

  const handleScroll = (scroll: UIEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    if (
      scroll.currentTarget.id === 'header' &&
      totalScrollRef.current &&
      listScrollRef.current
    ) {
      totalScrollRef.current.scrollLeft = scroll.currentTarget.scrollLeft;
      listScrollRef.current.scrollLeft = scroll.currentTarget.scrollLeft;
    }
    if (
      scroll.currentTarget.id === 'total' &&
      headerScrollRef.current &&
      listScrollRef.current
    ) {
      headerScrollRef.current.scrollLeft = scroll.currentTarget.scrollLeft;
      listScrollRef.current.scrollLeft = scroll.currentTarget.scrollLeft;
    }
    if (
      scroll.currentTarget.id === 'list' &&
      totalScrollRef.current &&
      headerScrollRef.current
    ) {
      headerScrollRef.current.scrollLeft = scroll.currentTarget.scrollLeft;
      totalScrollRef.current.scrollLeft = scroll.currentTarget.scrollLeft;
    }
  };

  if (graphType === 'AreaGraph') {
    return (
      <AreaGraph
        style={graphStyle}
        compact={compact}
        data={data}
        balanceTypeOp={balanceTypeOp}
        viewLabels={viewLabels}
        showTooltip={showTooltip}
      />
    );
  }
  if (graphType === 'BarGraph') {
    return (
      <BarGraph
        style={graphStyle}
        compact={compact}
        data={data}
        filters={filters}
        groupBy={groupBy}
        balanceTypeOp={balanceTypeOp}
        viewLabels={viewLabels}
        showHiddenCategories={showHiddenCategories}
        showOffBudget={showOffBudget}
        showTooltip={showTooltip}
      />
    );
  }
  if (graphType === 'BarLineGraph') {
    return (
      <BarLineGraph
        style={graphStyle}
        compact={compact}
        data={data}
        showTooltip={showTooltip}
      />
    );
  }
  if (graphType === 'DonutGraph') {
    return (
      <DonutGraph
        style={graphStyle}
        data={data}
        filters={filters}
        groupBy={groupBy}
        balanceTypeOp={balanceTypeOp}
        viewLabels={viewLabels}
        showHiddenCategories={showHiddenCategories}
        showOffBudget={showOffBudget}
        showTooltip={showTooltip}
      />
    );
  }
  if (graphType === 'LineGraph') {
    return (
      <LineGraph
        style={graphStyle}
        compact={compact}
        data={data}
        filters={filters}
        groupBy={groupBy}
        balanceTypeOp={balanceTypeOp}
        showHiddenCategories={showHiddenCategories}
        showOffBudget={showOffBudget}
        showTrendLines={showTrendLines}
        showTooltip={showTooltip}
        interval={interval}
      />
    );
  }
  if (graphType === 'StackedBarGraph') {
    return (
      <StackedBarGraph
        style={graphStyle}
        compact={compact}
        data={data}
        filters={filters}
        viewLabels={viewLabels}
        balanceTypeOp={balanceTypeOp}
        groupBy={groupBy}
        showHiddenCategories={showHiddenCategories}
        showOffBudget={showOffBudget}
        showTooltip={showTooltip}
        interval={interval}
      />
    );
  }
  if (graphType === 'TableGraph') {
    return (
      <ReportTable
        saveScrollWidth={saveScrollWidth}
        headerScrollRef={headerScrollRef}
        listScrollRef={listScrollRef}
        totalScrollRef={totalScrollRef}
        handleScroll={handleScroll}
        balanceTypeOp={balanceTypeOp}
        groupBy={groupBy}
        data={data}
        filters={filters}
        mode={mode}
        intervalsCount={intervalsCount}
        interval={interval}
        compact={compact}
        style={rowStyle}
        compactStyle={compactStyle}
        showHiddenCategories={showHiddenCategories}
        showOffBudget={showOffBudget}
      />
    );
  }
  return null;
}

import React from 'react';
import type { CSSProperties, ReactNode } from 'react';

import { theme } from '@actual-app/components/theme';
import { View } from '@actual-app/components/view';
import type { DataEntity, GroupedEntity } from '@actual-app/core/types/models';

import { Row } from '#components/table';

import { RenderTableRow } from './RenderTableRow';
import type { renderRowProps } from './ReportTable';

type ReportTableListProps = {
  data: DataEntity;
  mode: string;
  groupBy: string;
  renderRow: (arg: renderRowProps) => ReactNode;
  style?: CSSProperties;
};

export function ReportTableList({
  data,
  mode,
  groupBy,
  renderRow,
  style,
}: ReportTableListProps) {
  const metadata: GroupedEntity[] | undefined =
    groupBy === 'Category'
      ? data.groupedData || []
      : groupBy === 'Interval'
        ? data.intervalData.map(interval => {
            return {
              id: '',
              name: '',
              date: interval.date,
              totalAssets: interval.totalAssets,
              totalDebts: interval.totalDebts,
              netAssets: interval.netAssets,
              netDebts: interval.netDebts,
              totalTotals: interval.totalTotals,
              totalBudgeted: interval.totalBudgeted,
              totalSpent: interval.totalSpent,
              intervalData: [],
              categories: [],
            };
          })
        : data.data;

  return (
    <View>
      {metadata ? (
        <View>
          {metadata.map((item, index) => {
            return (
              <View key={index}>
                <RenderTableRow
                  index={index}
                  renderRow={renderRow}
                  mode={mode}
                  metadata={metadata}
                  style={{
                    ...(item.categories && {
                      color: theme.tableRowHeaderText,
                      backgroundColor: theme.tableRowHeaderBackground,
                      fontWeight: 600,
                    }),
                    ...style,
                  }}
                />
                {item.categories && (
                  <>
                    <View>
                      {item.categories.map(
                        (category: GroupedEntity, i: number) => {
                          return (
                            <View key={category.id}>
                              <RenderTableRow
                                index={i}
                                renderRow={renderRow}
                                mode={mode}
                                metadata={metadata}
                                parent_index={index}
                                style={style}
                              />
                              {category.subcategories?.map(subcategory => (
                                <View
                                  key={
                                    subcategory.isUnallocated
                                      ? `${subcategory.id}-unallocated`
                                      : subcategory.id
                                  }
                                >
                                  {renderRow({
                                    item: subcategory,
                                    mode,
                                    style,
                                    isSubcategory: true,
                                  })}
                                </View>
                              ))}
                            </View>
                          );
                        },
                      )}
                    </View>
                    <Row height={20} />
                  </>
                )}
              </View>
            );
          })}
        </View>
      ) : (
        <View width="flex" />
      )}
    </View>
  );
}

import { theme } from '@actual-app/components/theme';
import type {
  balanceTypeOpType,
  GroupedEntity,
  IntervalEntity,
  LegendEntity,
} from '@actual-app/core/types/models';

import { getColorScale } from '#components/reports/chart-theme';

export function calculateLegend(
  intervalData: IntervalEntity[],
  calcDataFiltered: GroupedEntity[],
  groupBy: string,
  graphType?: string,
  balanceTypeOp?: balanceTypeOpType,
): LegendEntity[] {
  const colorScale = getColorScale('qualitative');
  const chooseData =
    groupBy === 'Interval'
      ? intervalData.map(c => {
          return { name: c.date, id: null, data: c };
        })
      : calcDataFiltered.map(c => {
          return { name: c.name, id: c.id, data: c };
        });

  function getColor(data: IntervalEntity | GroupedEntity, index: number) {
    if (graphType === 'DonutGraph') {
      return colorScale[index % colorScale.length];
    }

    if (groupBy === 'Interval') {
      if (balanceTypeOp === 'totalDebts') {
        return theme.reportsNumberNegative;
      }

      if (balanceTypeOp === 'netDebts') {
        return theme.reportsNumberNegative;
      }

      if (
        balanceTypeOp === 'totalTotals' ||
        balanceTypeOp === 'totalBudgeted'
      ) {
        const total =
          balanceTypeOp === 'totalBudgeted'
            ? data.totalBudgeted
            : data.totalTotals;

        if (total < 0) {
          return theme.reportsNumberNegative;
        }

        return theme.reportsNumberPositive;
      }

      if (balanceTypeOp === 'totalAssets' || balanceTypeOp === 'netAssets') {
        return theme.reportsNumberPositive;
      }

      return theme.reportsChartFill;
    }

    return colorScale[index % colorScale.length];
  }

  const legend: LegendEntity[] = chooseData.map((item, index) => {
    return {
      id: item.id || '',
      name: item.name || '',
      color: getColor(item.data, index),
      dataKey: item.id || item.name || '', // Use id for unique data lookup
      uncategorizedId:
        'uncategorizedId' in item.data ? item.data.uncategorizedId : undefined,
    };
  });
  return legend;
}

const buildColorMap = (
  groupedData: GroupedEntity[],
  legend: LegendEntity[],
): Map<string, string> => {
  const legendById = new Map(
    legend
      .filter(l => l.id != null)
      .map(l => [l.id, resolveCSSVariable(l.color)]),
  );

  return groupedData.reduce((acc, group) => {
    if (!group.id) return acc;

    const groupColor = legendById.get(group.id);
    if (!groupColor) return acc;

    acc.set(group.id, groupColor);

    // Fix 1: capture cats once to avoid group.categories.length on undefined
    const cats = group.categories ?? [];
    cats.forEach((cat, i) => {
      if (!cat.id) return;
      const shade = 0.15 + (i / Math.max(cats.length, 1)) * 0.5;
      acc.set(cat.id, shadeColor(groupColor, shade));
    });

    return acc;
  }, new Map<string, string>());
};

import type { CategoryEntity } from '#types/models';

export type CategoryWithSubcategories<T extends CategoryEntity> = T & {
  subcategories: T[];
};

/**
 * Turns a group's flat category list into top-level categories, each with
 * its subcategories. Order is kept within each level. A subcategory is
 * shown as a top-level category when its parent isn't in the list
 * (deleted or in another group) or is itself a subcategory, which the
 * server doesn't allow but conflicting edits from two devices could
 * produce. That way a category never disappears.
 */
export function nestCategories<T extends CategoryEntity>(
  categories: T[],
): CategoryWithSubcategories<T>[] {
  const ids = new Set(categories.map(cat => cat.id));
  const hasValidParent = (cat: T) =>
    cat.parent_id != null && ids.has(cat.parent_id);
  const parentIds = new Set(
    categories.filter(cat => !hasValidParent(cat)).map(cat => cat.id),
  );
  const subcategoriesByParent = new Map<CategoryEntity['id'], T[]>();
  const topLevel: T[] = [];

  for (const cat of categories) {
    if (cat.parent_id && parentIds.has(cat.parent_id)) {
      const siblings = subcategoriesByParent.get(cat.parent_id) ?? [];
      siblings.push(cat);
      subcategoriesByParent.set(cat.parent_id, siblings);
    } else {
      topLevel.push(cat);
    }
  }

  return topLevel.map(cat => ({
    ...cat,
    subcategories: subcategoriesByParent.get(cat.id) ?? [],
  }));
}

/** Whether a category is a subcategory of another category. */
export function isSubcategory(category: Pick<CategoryEntity, 'parent_id'>) {
  return category.parent_id != null;
}

const food = { id: 'food', name: 'Food', group: 'g-food', sort_order: 1 };
const restaurants = {
  id: 'restaurants',
  name: 'Restaurants',
  group: 'g-food',
  parent_id: 'food',
  sort_order: 2,
};
const groceries = {
  id: 'groceries',
  name: 'Groceries',
  group: 'g-food',
  parent_id: 'food',
  sort_order: 3,
};
const rent = { id: 'rent', name: 'Rent', group: 'g-bills', sort_order: 4 };

function makeCategories(
  overrides: Partial<Record<string, Partial<CategoryEntity>>> = {},
) {
  const withOverrides = (cat: CategoryEntity) => ({
    ...cat,
    ...overrides[cat.id],
  });
  const grouped = [
    {
      id: 'g-food',
      name: 'Food',
      sort_order: 1,
      categories: [food, restaurants, groceries].map(withOverrides),
    },
    {
      id: 'g-bills',
      name: 'Bills',
      sort_order: 2,
      categories: [rent].map(withOverrides),
    },
  ] satisfies CategoryGroupEntity[];
  return { grouped, list: grouped.flatMap(group => group.categories) };
}

function row(
  category: CategoryEntity,
  amount: number,
  hidden = false,
): QueryDataEntity {
  return {
    date: '2026-09',
    category: category.id,
    categoryHidden: hidden,
    categoryGroup: category.group,
    categoryGroupHidden: false,
    account: 'checking',
    accountOffBudget: false,
    payee: '',
    transferAccount: '',
    amount,
  };
}

// Spent this month: Food directly 10, Restaurants 30, Groceries 50, Rent 100.
const spending = [
  row(food, -1000),
  row(restaurants, -3000),
  row(groceries, -5000),
  row(rent, -10000),
];

const options = {
  startDate: '2026-09-01',
  endDate: '2026-09-30',
  interval: 'Monthly',
  conditions: [],
  conditionsOp: 'and',
  showEmpty: false,
  showOffBudget: false,
  showHiddenCategories: false,
  showUncategorized: false,
  trimIntervals: false,
  // Keeps budget order, so groups and categories come out as listed.
  sortByOp: 'budget' as const,
};

const spreadsheet = {} as ReturnType<typeof useSpreadsheet>;

async function runGrouped(
  categories: ReturnType<typeof makeCategories>,
  balanceTypeOp: 'totalDebts' | 'totalBudgeted' = 'totalDebts',
  conditions: RuleConditionEntity[] = [],
) {
  let result: GroupedEntity[] = [];
  await createGroupedSpreadsheet({
    ...options,
    categories,
    balanceTypeOp,
    conditions,
  })(spreadsheet, data => (result = data));
  return result;
}

async function runCustom(
  categories: ReturnType<typeof makeCategories>,
  balanceTypeOp: 'totalDebts' | 'totalBudgeted' = 'totalDebts',
) {
  let result: DataEntity | undefined;
  await createCustomSpreadsheet({
    ...options,
    categories,
    groupBy: 'Category',
    balanceTypeOp,
  })(spreadsheet, data => (result = data));
  return result;
}

function byId(rows: GroupedEntity[] | undefined, id: string) {
  return rows?.find(r => r.id === id && !r.isUnallocated);
}

  it('rolls subcategories into their parent without counting them twice', async () => {
    const [foodGroup] = await runGrouped(makeCategories());

    // The group counts every transaction exactly once.

    // Only the parent is a top-level row, and it includes its children.
    expect(foodGroup.categories?.map(c => c.id)).toEqual(['food']);
    const foodRow = byId(foodGroup.categories, 'food');
    expect(foodRow?.totalDebts).toBe(-9000);

    // Adding up the top-level rows gives the group total again.
    const topLevelSum = (foodGroup.categories ?? []).reduce(
      (sum, c) => sum + c.totalDebts,
      0,
    );
    expect(topLevelSum).toBe(foodGroup.totalDebts);

export function filterEmptyRows({
  showEmpty,
  data,
  balanceTypeOp = 'totalDebts',
}: {
  showEmpty: boolean;
  data: GroupedEntity;
  balanceTypeOp?: balanceTypeOpType;
}): boolean {
  let showHide: boolean;
  if (balanceTypeOp === 'totalTotals' || balanceTypeOp === 'totalBudgeted') {
    showHide =
      data['totalDebts'] !== 0 ||
      data['totalAssets'] !== 0 ||
      data[balanceTypeOp] !== 0 ||
      (data.totalSpent ?? 0) !== 0;
  } else {
    showHide = data[balanceTypeOp] !== 0;
  }
  return !showEmpty ? showHide : true;
}

Transactions can be filtered for a certain period of time using **Range**. **Live Date** filters show transaction data dynamically, for instance during the current month (This month). For a fixed time frame, **Static Date** filters will show transactions between two dates.

### Options

Under Options, reports behavior can be changed

- `Show hidden categories` will enable Categories marked as hidden in the Budget page.
- `Show empty rows` will show items chosen in Split with 0 value.
- `Show off budget` enables two categories:
  - Transfers: include all transfers across on budget account. Transfers from on budget to off budget are not counted.
  - Off budget: include all transactions in off budget accounts. Transfers from on budget to off budget are not counted.
- `Show uncategorized` will show transactions which have not been assigned a category.

Single Categories or entire Groups can be excluded from the Report by using the list on the bottom left side.
Grayed out options in dropdown menus are not yet available for the chosen report.

## Center Menu

Icons in the first group of the center menu are used to select the displayed report, the second group is used to show graph legends, summary and labels. The funnel icon can be used to [filter transactions](../transactions/filters.md). Finally, the menu on the right-hand side is used to Save a Custom Report to the Reports page.

# Plan: fix issue #100 (custom reports ignore unchecked subcategories and never show them on their own)

Paths below are relative to `/Users/james/ActualBudget/actual-budget`. Line numbers are approximate.

## Approach

1. **Keep the selector's own category filter exactly as written.** A new helper, `expandReportConditions`, skips the family expansion for the single category condition the selector owns. Any other category condition still gets expanded. Custom reports and `showActivity` use the new helper. Spending, cash flow and the other reports keep calling `includeSubcategoriesInConditions` and don't change.
2. **One rule decides which subs roll into which parent.** It works by narrowing the existing `subcategoryIdsByParent` map, so `getRolledUpCategoryIds` and `getNestedSubcategoryIds` keep their signatures and just receive the narrower map. A sub rolls into its parent only when the toggle is off and either nothing is filtered or both the parent and the sub are checked. Otherwise the sub gets its own row. Every sub ends up in exactly one row, so it is never counted twice and never lost.
3. **Each row records the category ids it adds up** in a new `GroupedEntity.categoryIds` field. Click-through uses those ids, so the transactions shown always match the row. This replaces the `includeSubcategories` flag.

### Changes to existing behaviour and caveats

- **Typed filters behave differently.** A filter typed by hand as `Category is Food` now covers Food only, not Food plus its subs. The selector already displays it that way (subs unchecked). Two existing tests in `subcategories.test.ts` (L440, L460) will change because of this. Saved reports built with the selector are not affected: ticking a parent always saves the whole family.
- **"Or" filters.** When conditions are joined with "or", an unchecked sub can still be pulled in by another condition (a payee, say). Its amounts then show in the sub's own row, the same way unchecked top-level categories already behave today.
- **"Show empty rows".** With it on, unchecked subs can now appear as zero rows, the same as unchecked top-level categories do now.
- **Dashboard clicks ignore the report's filters.** `GetCardData` never passes `filters` to `ChooseGraph`. That is not new and stays out of scope. With `categoryIds`, the categories in a dashboard click-through are still correct.

---

## Per-file changes

### Shared logic: `packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/subcategories.ts`

New exports, written with the file's usual comment style:

- **`isComplexCategoryCondition(conditions)`**: the logic moved verbatim from `CustomReport.tsx` L200-217. It returns true when any category condition uses contains, doesNotContain, matches, hasTags or hasAnyTag; when there are 2 or more category conditions; or when there is any `category_group` condition.
- **`getSelectorCategoryCondition(conditions)`**: returns the single category condition when the conditions are not complex and its op is is, isNot, oneOf or notOneOf. Otherwise it returns `undefined`.
- **`getSelectedCategoryIds(conditions, categoryList): Set<string> | undefined`**: the same switch as `useSelectedCategories` (CustomReport L87-110). It returns `undefined` ("everything selected") when there is no selector condition.
- **`expandReportConditions(conditions, categoryGroups)`**: maps the conditions in their original order. The selector condition passes through as the same object; everything else goes through `expandSubcategoryConditions`. Order matters because tests check the exact `make-filters-from-conditions` payload.
- **`getRolledUpSubcategoryIdsByParent(subcategoryIdsByParent, { showSubcategories, selectedCategoryIds })`**: builds a new map from the existing one, keeping only the subs that roll in. A sub `s` of parent `P` stays in when the toggle is off and either nothing is filtered or both `P` and `s` are checked. Parents left with no subs are removed, so `getRolledUpCategoryIds` returns `undefined` for them.
- **`sortSubcategoriesUnderParents(rows, compare, subcategoryIdsByParent)`**: used for the table when the toggle is on.
  - It sorts the top-level rows with `compare`.
  - It places each parent's sub rows, also sorted, directly after the parent and marks them `isSubcategory: true`.
  - A sub whose parent has no row (for example, an empty parent hidden by `filterEmptyRows`) is sorted with the top-level rows and is not marked.
- Update the comments on `getRolledUpCategoryIds`, `getNestedSubcategoryIds` and `expandSubcategoryConditions` to say they now take the narrowed map and apply to filters outside the selector.

### Row types: `packages/loot-core/src/types/models/reports.ts`

- `CustomReportEntity` (around L19): add `showSubcategories: boolean;`.
- `CustomReportData` (around L163): add `show_subcategories: number;`.
- `GroupedEntity` (around L120-145), each with a comment:
  - `categoryIds?: string[]`: the categories this row adds up. It is only set when that is more than its own id.
  - `isSubcategory?: boolean`: a subcategory row shown on its own under its parent in the table.
- Update the `subcategories` comment: it is filled only for parents whose subs are rolled in, so the toggle is off.

### `packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/recalculate.ts`

- In the return (around L117), add `...(categoryIds && { categoryIds })`.
- Reword the comment at L25-27.

### `packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/custom-spreadsheet.ts`

- Props type (L48-69): add `showSubcategories?: boolean`. Destructure it with a default of `false`.
- L100-111:

  ```ts

  const subcategoryIdsByParent = getRolledUpSubcategoryIdsByParent(allSubcategoryIdsByParent, {
    showSubcategories,
    selectedCategoryIds: getSelectedCategoryIds(conditions, categories.list),
  });
  ```

- L134: `expandSubcategoryConditions` becomes `expandReportConditions`.

# Fix #100: custom reports ignore unchecked subcategories

## Context

In custom reports grouped by category, unchecking a subcategory in the category selector doesn't remove its amount, and a subcategory is never shown on its own. Causes (confirmed by reading code):

1. `expandSubcategoryConditions` (`spreadsheets/subcategories.ts:93`) turns the selector's `oneOf [parent]` back into `oneOf [parent, ...all subs]`, so unchecked subs are fetched again (custom-spreadsheet.ts:134, grouped-spreadsheet.ts:61, and budgeted mode through the same conditions).
2. Parent rows always roll in every sub (`getRolledUpCategoryIds`, grouped-spreadsheet.ts:173), and every sub is dropped as a row (`getNestedSubcategoryIds`), so a checked sub whose parent is unchecked shows under the parent's name, and subs can never be their own bar/slice/line.
3. Click-through (`graphs/showActivity.ts:63-70, 104`) re-adds all subs and re-expands the filters.

Decisions (from the user):
- A saved **"Show subcategories"** report option, **off by default**, so existing reports look the same.
- A checked sub whose parent is unchecked gets **its own row**, even with the option off.
- In custom reports, the single selector-owned category condition is applied **as written**. Other reports (Spending, Cash Flow, …) keep including the family.

## Approach

**One rule decides roll-up.** Narrow the existing `subcategoryIdsByParent` map before it reaches the row builders. A sub rolls into its parent only when the option is off **and** either nothing is filtered or both parent and sub are checked. Otherwise the sub is its own row and the parent row covers only its own id. Every sub is in exactly one row, so totals never double count. `getRolledUpCategoryIds`/`getNestedSubcategoryIds` keep their signatures and just get the narrowed map.

**Rows carry their ids.** `recalculate` returns `categoryIds` on the row. Click-through uses them instead of `includeSubcategories`, so the transactions match the row.

## Changes

### `packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/subcategories.ts`
New exports, written in the file's comment style:
- `isComplexCategoryCondition(conditions)`: moved verbatim from `CustomReport.tsx:200-217`.
- `getSelectorCategoryCondition(conditions)`: the single is/isNot/oneOf/notOneOf category condition when not complex, else `undefined`.
- `getSelectedCategoryIds(conditions, categoryList): Set<string> | undefined`: the switch from `useSelectedCategories` (`CustomReport.tsx:87-110`); `undefined` means everything is selected.
- `expandReportConditions(conditions, categoryGroups)`: keeps the order, passes the selector condition through unchanged, and runs the rest through `expandSubcategoryConditions`.
- `getRolledUpSubcategoryIdsByParent(map, { showSubcategories, selectedCategoryIds })`: the narrowing rule above, which drops parents left with no subs.
- `sortSubcategoriesUnderParents(rows, compare, allSubcategoryIdsByParent)`: for the table with the option on.
  - Sorts the top-level rows.
  - Places each parent's sorted subs right after it, marked `isSubcategory: true`.
  - A sub whose parent has no row is sorted as a top-level row.
- Update the existing comments to match.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-27 23:42:57Z)**_

These are rough estimates from reading the code; I haven't prototyped any of the options.

## The current plan

- **Size:** about 20 source files plus a migration, 3 test files, a docs page and a release note. My guess is roughly 600–900 changed lines, about half of them tests.
- **What makes it big:** the saved toggle (migration, loot-core types and mapping, sidebar, CustomReport state, dashboard widgets) and moving click-through to `categoryIds` across five graph components.
- **The actual bug fix is small:** applying the selector's filter as written plus the narrowing rule is about 3 files.

## Alternatives

**A. Bug fix only (smallest)**
- Changes: `subcategories.ts` (`expandReportConditions` and the narrowing rule), the two spreadsheets, and the `ReportTableRow` click-through.
- Size: about 5 files, 150–250 lines with tests, no migration and no UI.
- Covers acceptance criteria 1 and 4 (unchecked subcategories removed, totals correct).
- It doesn't let you see a subcategory as its own bar. However, the Table view already nests subcategory rows under their parent (`grouped-spreadsheet.ts:172-190`, `ReportTableList.tsx:98`), so subcategories can already be compared there.
- Lowest risk. It's also the first step of every other option.

**B. Multi-coloured (segmented) parent bars**
- Each parent bar is split into a coloured segment per subcategory, plus one for the parent's own transactions.
- Size: similar to the current plan or larger, but the work moves from plumbing into graph code.
- It still needs A underneath, because segments don't fix the filtering.
- Spreadsheets: rows need per-subcategory segment values. Recharts stacks by shared `dataKey`s, so every row needs keys like `sub:<id>`, mostly empty.
- `BarGraph.tsx`: switch from one `Bar` with per-row `Cell`s to several stacked `Bar`s, with shades derived from the parent's colour. Tooltip, legend and click handling then work per segment.
- It only works well for Bar, and possibly Donut (a parent/sub ring like the existing group ring). Stacked Bar already stacks categories over time, and segments inside segments don't work; Line and Area have no equivalent. That conflicts with criterion 5 (the same behaviour across all graph types).
- Visual regression snapshots would change and need regenerating in Docker.
- No migration if it's always on, but changing every report's look by default is a big UX shift, so you'd probably want a toggle anyway.

**C. Current plan with an unsaved toggle**
- Drops the migration and loot-core changes, about 5 files fewer.
- Dashboard widgets can't use it, which weakens criterion 5.

## Recommendation

Do **A first as its own PR**. It's small and easy to review, it fixes the reported bug, and the Table view already covers most of the "see each subcategory" need. Then decide between the current plan's toggle (B') and segmented bars (B) as a follow-up. The toggle works for every graph type and fits the acceptance criteria better. Segmented bars look better for Bar and Donut but don't carry over to the other graph types.

If you want, I can rewrite the plan file as a two-phase plan: A now, the toggle as phase 2.

# Fix #100 (part A): unchecked subcategories still counted in custom reports

## Context

In a custom report grouped by category, unchecking a subcategory in the category selector doesn't remove its amount; it is still added into the parent's row. If the parent is unchecked and a subcategory is checked, the subcategory's amount shows under the parent's name.

This is the minimal bug fix (acceptance criteria 1 and 4). Showing every subcategory as its own bar via a "Show subcategories" option is a later follow-up. The Table view already nests subcategory rows under their parent.

**Causes**
1. **The filter is widened.** `CustomReport.tsx:219-264` stores the checkboxes as one `category oneOf [checked ids]` condition. `expandSubcategoryConditions` (`spreadsheets/subcategories.ts:93`) then adds every subcategory of any listed parent back in. This happens in `custom-spreadsheet.ts:134` and `grouped-spreadsheet.ts:61`, and Budgeted mode uses the same conditions.
2. **Parent rows include every subcategory.** `getRolledUpCategoryIds`/`getNestedSubcategoryIds` (custom) and `grouped-spreadsheet.ts:149-173` always put every subcategory into the parent row, whether it is checked or not.

**Agreed behaviour:** in custom reports, the single category condition shown by the checkboxes is applied exactly as written. A checked subcategory whose parent is unchecked gets its own row. Other reports (Spending, Cash Flow, …) keep including subcategories.

## Changes

### `packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/subcategories.ts`
Add these, in the file's existing comment style:
- `isComplexCategoryCondition(conditions)`: moved verbatim from `CustomReport.tsx:200-217`. It is true for contains/doesNotContain/matches/hasTags-style category ops, for 2 or more category conditions, or for any `category_group` condition.
- `getSelectorCategoryCondition(conditions)`: returns the single `is`/`isNot`/`oneOf`/`notOneOf` category condition when the conditions aren't complex, otherwise `undefined`.
- `getSelectedCategoryIds(conditions, categoryList): Set<string> | undefined`: the switch logic from `useSelectedCategories` (`CustomReport.tsx:82-113`). `undefined` means all categories are selected.
- `expandReportConditions(conditions, categoryGroups)`: maps the conditions in order. The selector condition passes through unchanged, and every other condition goes through `expandSubcategoryConditions`.
- `getRolledUpSubcategoryIdsByParent(subcategoryIdsByParent, selectedCategoryIds)`: returns a narrowed copy of the map.
  - A subcategory stays under its parent only when `selectedCategoryIds` is `undefined` or contains both the parent and the subcategory.
  - A parent left with no subcategories is dropped.
  - Because of this, a checked subcategory whose parent is unchecked is no longer a nested id, so it gets its own row.
- `getRolledUpCategoryIds` and `getNestedSubcategoryIds` don't change. Their callers pass the narrowed map; update their comments to say so.

### `spreadsheets/custom-spreadsheet.ts`
- Lines 100-111: build the map with `getRolledUpSubcategoryIdsByParent(getSubcategoryIdsByParent(categories.grouped), getSelectedCategoryIds(conditions, categories.list))`, and update the comment. `rowItems`, the `getRolledUpCategoryIds` calls and the totals stay as they are.
- Line 134: `expandSubcategoryConditions` becomes `expandReportConditions`.

### `spreadsheets/grouped-spreadsheet.ts`
- Lines 49-50: narrow the map the same way.
- Line 61: use `expandReportConditions`.
- Lines 142-190 don't change. With the narrowed map, a parent's nested `subcategories` lists only its checked subcategories, and a subcategory checked without its parent becomes its own entry in `categories`. Update the comment.

### `graphs/showActivity.ts`
- Line 104: use `expandReportConditions(filters, categories.grouped)`.
- The drilldown still uses `oneOf [parent, ...all subs]`. The accounts page combines it with the report filter, which is now applied as written, so unchecked subcategories drop out and the transaction list matches the row.
- Update the comment.

### `reports/CustomReport.tsx`
Use the shared helpers so the checkboxes and the spreadsheets read the condition the same way:
- `useSelectedCategories` (lines 73-114) uses `getSelectedCategoryIds`.
- `isComplexCategoryCondition` (lines 204-217) calls the helper, imported under a different name so it doesn't clash with the local variable.

### Release note
Add `upcoming-release-notes/custom-report-unchecked-subcategories.md` in the Bugfixes category, using the `writing-release-notes` skill.

## Known behaviour change
In custom reports, a single typed filter such as `Category is Food` now covers Food only, not its subcategories. This matches what the checkboxes already show, which is Food ticked and its subcategories unticked. The existing tests that expect the whole family are rewritten.

## Tests

### `spreadsheets/subcategories.test.ts`
Fixture amounts: Food 10, Restaurants 30, Groceries 50, Rent 100.
- **Helper tests**
  - `isComplexCategoryCondition`.
  - `getSelectedCategoryIds` for is, isNot, oneOf, notOneOf, no condition, and a complex condition (which returns `undefined`).
  - `expandReportConditions`:
    - a lone `oneOf [food]` is left unchanged;
    - when a second category condition is present, both are expanded;
    - non-category conditions and the original order are kept.
  - `getRolledUpSubcategoryIdsByParent` for no filter, parent plus one subcategory, and a subcategory only.
- **Rewrite** the tests at line 440 ("filters spending reports on the whole family") and line 460 (Budgeted, filtered on the parent). The selector condition is now passed through as written. Add a case where a complex condition is still expanded.
- **Behaviour tests**, run for both `runCustom` and `runGrouped` (extend `runCustom` to accept `conditions` if needed). Check the totals, each interval's totals and the `stacked` keys:

  | Filter | Expected rows | Expected total |
  |---|---|---|
  | `oneOf [food, groceries]` | Food row only (Food + Groceries) | -6000 |
  | `oneOf [restaurants]` | Restaurants as its own row, no Food row | -3000 |
  | no filter | Food rolls up all three | unchanged |

- **Grouped:** Food's `subcategories` lists Groceries and the "Not in a subcategory" row, but not Restaurants.
- **Budgeted** with `oneOf [food, groceries]`: the Restaurants budget is left out.
- The existing roll-up tests (lines 207-310) must still pass.

### `graphs/showActivity.test.ts`
- Line 194: change it so a lone report filter `is food` passes through as written.
- Add a case where a complex filter (two category conditions) is still expanded.

## Verification
1. From the repo root, run `yarn typecheck`, `yarn lint:fix` and `yarn test`.
2. Run `yarn start`, choose "Don't use a server", then "View demo". On the budget page, add a subcategory under a category. Add transactions to both the parent and the subcategory.
3. In a new custom report grouped by Category, check each of these on Bar, Donut and Table:
   - Unchecking the subcategory lowers the parent's total by the subcategory's amount, and the report total drops by the same amount.
   - Unchecking the parent while the subcategory stays checked shows the subcategory as its own row.
   - Clicking the parent's bar or row lists only the checked categories' transactions.
   - Spending and Cash Flow reports filtered on the parent still include its subcategories.

    const groupedDataFiltered = groupedData.filter(i =>
      filterEmptyRows({ showEmpty, data: i, balanceTypeOp }),
    );

    // Determine interval range across all groups and their nested categories
    const allGroupsForTrimming: GroupedEntity[] = [];
    groupedDataFiltered.forEach(group => {
      allGroupsForTrimming.push(group);
      if (group.categories) {
        allGroupsForTrimming.push(...group.categories);
      }
    });

    const { startIndex, endIndex } = determineIntervalRange(
      allGroupsForTrimming,
      groupedDataFiltered.length > 0 ? groupedDataFiltered[0].intervalData : [],
      trimIntervals,
      balanceTypeOp,
    );

    // Trim all groupedData intervals (including nested categories) based on the range
    trimGroupedDataIntervals(groupedDataFiltered, startIndex, endIndex);

    const sortedGroupedDataFiltered = [...groupedDataFiltered]
      .sort(sortData({ balanceTypeOp, sortByOp }))
      .map(g => {
        g.categories = [...(g.categories ?? [])].sort(
          sortData({ balanceTypeOp, sortByOp }),
        );
        return g;
      });

    setData(sortedGroupedDataFiltered);
  };
}

}

// The categories checked in the custom report's category selector, or
// undefined when every category is.
export function getSelectedCategoryIds(
  conditions: RuleConditionEntity[],
  categories: Pick<CategoryEntity, 'id'>[],
): Set<string> | undefined {
  const cond = getSelectorCategoryCondition(conditions);
  if (!cond) {
    return undefined;
  }
  const ids = new Set<string>(
    Array.isArray(cond.value) ? cond.value : [cond.value],
  );
  const excludes = cond.op === 'isNot' || cond.op === 'notOneOf';
  return new Set(
    categories.map(({ id }) => id).filter(id => ids.has(id) !== excludes),
  );
}

# Writing Release Notes for actualbudget/actual

Release notes are the user-facing changelog. Each code change adds one Markdown file to `upcoming-release-notes/`, and these get collected into the published changelog at the next release. The authoritative source is the **Writing Good Release Notes** section of `packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md`. Read it if anything below is unclear.

## The file

Create `upcoming-release-notes/<slug>.md`, where `<slug>` is a **short, descriptive kebab-case slug** naming the change (e.g. `add-payee-autocomplete.md`, `fix-mobile-category-delete.md`). Do **not** use a PR number, since the PR link is resolved automatically at release time. (Numeric filenames like `1234.md` still work, but a slug is preferred.)

```markdown
---
category: Features
authors: [YourGitHubUsername]
---

Add payee autocomplete to the transaction entry form
```

- **`category`**: exactly one of `Features` (new feature), `Enhancements` (improvement to an existing feature), `Bugfix` (bug fix), or `Maintenance` (internal change with no user-visible effect).
- **`authors`**: array of the GitHub username(s) who did the work.

## Writing the entry

The body is the changelog line. It is read by everyday users, not developers.

- **One sentence.** Short and clear. No paragraphs, no bullet lists, no long prose.
- **Plain language, no technical detail.** Describe what changed for the user, not how it was built. Avoid file names, function names, internal component names, and implementation jargon. (Exception: `Maintenance` entries may be technical, since they are for internal changes.)
- **Phrase it as a command.** Start with a present-tense verb: "Add …", "Fix …", "Show …", not "Added …" or "Adds …".
- Generally match the PR title, but reword it if that reads more clearly to a user.

Good: `Fix incorrect balance when reconciling an account with future transactions`
Too technical: `Fix off-by-one in reconcileTransactions() when txn.date > today`

<pasted_content id="a6d9">
## Description

Fixes test failures that show up when running `yarn test` locally, especially on Windows (#98, #94).

- **sync-server:** Test cleanup failed with `EBUSY` because `account.sqlite` was still open when the folder holding it was deleted. The down migration now closes the account database first.
- **loot-core `main.test.ts`:** Each test now closes the budget before deleting its files, for the same Windows reason.
- **loot-core `vitest.config.ts`:** Vitest now skips the copies of test files inside Stryker's `.stryker-tmp/` folder, and keeps its default exclude list.
- **desktop-client `mutations.test.tsx`:** The test now waits for i18next to finish starting up before rendering. Otherwise the hook could return `null` after running `yarn generate:i18n`.

All tests pass on Windows with no cleanup errors.

## Design Decisions

- **The database is closed in the migration, not the test cleanup.** A real down migration on Windows would hit the same `EBUSY` error, so fixing it in the migration covers both cases.
- **The connection is reset after it's closed.** `closeAccountDb()` clears the stored connection, so the next `getAccountDb()` call opens a fresh one instead of reusing a closed one.
- **The change is kept small.** No test files or shared database code were changed. Only the database that blocks the folder delete gets closed.


## UML Diagram
Not applicable for this specific PR as it simply fixes failing test cases..

## Tech Debt

**Introduced**
- `account-db.js` is still plain JavaScript, so the new `closeAccountDb()` helper is untyped.
- The `create-folders` down migration now depends on `account-db.js`. Before, it only deleted folders.

**Encountered**
- The shared account database connection is never closed anywhere else, including when the server shuts down.
- If the test cleanup fails, it leaves stale files behind (`.migrate-test` and `test-server-files/`). They have to be deleted by hand before the tests will run again.
- Tests that are expected to fail log real-looking errors (`Error parsing sync request`, `Invalid Origin header`), which makes the test output hard to read.

## Related issue(s)

Closes issue #98 and issue #94 

## Testing

This fixes our failed vitests, so I verified by re-running all failed tests to verify they now pass.

## Checklist

- [X] Release notes added (see link above)
- [X] No obvious regressions in affected areas
- [X] Self-review has been performed - I have read every line of this diff and can explain what each change does and why it is needed
